scope: Original stalled-position accounting for finite ordinary recovery
finding: Each recovery transition refreshed progressPosition. FINAL forward retry could travel3m from its reverse endpoint and reset recovery while still behind its original stalled position. Repeating rear/forward motion could therefore replenish the supposedly finite command budget without clearing the obstruction.
implementation: The original journal captures one finite ATL progressAnchor. Same-group/same-route stage records preserve it together with the existing hard deadline, including after owner adoption. Stage-local origin and movement clocks remain separate. Route-progress credit compares current waypoint distance against this anchor, requiring3m beyond the original stalled position plus existing movement/safety constraints. Missing/malformed inherited anchor remains empty and grants no reset; it is not minted from a later reverse endpoint. New authored route remains a separate episode.
sourceRelation: Continues the retained HBQ smooth rear recovery intent without copying renewable pushes or treating any displacement as success. The original-deadline/owner-local native command policy is CBE-specific; no whole-source parity claim.
cost: One bounded three-number journal field and constant metadata/distance checks at existing stage callbacks. No world query, scheduler, route rewrite, native movement command or increased retry/deadline.

validation.fullPipeline: Passed1476 existing tests and complete build gates after final normalization; .qa/cbe-recovery-progress-anchor-build.log

limits: Waypoint-distance progress remains an approximation on curved routes; this change does not introduce a route-arc metric. Registered convoy following is unchanged. Queue crossing, native leaf phases and handback remain incomplete.
